description: A bright, airy living room with a steeply pitched cathedral ceiling photographed at standing eye-level, approximately five feet off the floor, using a normal lens and a centered symmetrical composition facing the fireplace wall. The ceiling is white-painted shiplap between exposed structural oak beams in a warm honey-blond tone, converging at the gable ridge. Two black curtain rods flank the upper corners, with floor-length ivory linen sheers framing large black-framed windows on both sides. The fireplace surround and mantel are white Carrara marble with fine grey veining, its form simple and rectilinear. Flanking the fireplace are built-in open shelving niches with white-painted surfaces, populated with an artful arrangement of terracotta and unglazed ceramic vessels of varying shapes and sizes, plus a small vase of delicate dry-branch stems. A square framed abstract art print in bold black brushstrokes on white paper hangs centered above the mantel. The firebox contains neatly stacked cut log rounds for fire-ready ambiance, and additional log stacks fill the bottom shelf of each built-in niche. The seating arrangement consists of a large ivory linen upholstered sofa on the right and a pair of oversized rounded boucle swivel chairs in warm caramel on the left, both surrounding a solid oak rectangular coffee table with a lower shelf. On the coffee table: a single white ceramic vase with sparse flowering stems, a turned wood bowl, and stacked books. A creamy jute area rug anchors the grouping. A small ornamental olive tree in a simple pot stands to the right. The palette is crisp white, warm honey oak, caramel boucle, ivory, and terracotta ceramics.
